questions.text:
Let p, q, r denote the statements "It is raining ," It is cold", and " It is pleasant,"
respectively. Then the statement "It is not raining and it is pleasant, and it is not pleasant
only if it is raining and it is cold" is represented by
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- "It is not raining and it is pleasant": [latex] eg p\wedge r[/latex]
- "It is not pleasant only if it is raining and cold": "A only if B" means [latex]A ightarrow B[/latex], so [latex] eg r ightarrow(p\wedge q)[/latex]

Joined by "and": [latex]( eg p\wedge r)\wedge( eg r ightarrow(p\wedge q))[/latex]

Answer: Option 1

questions.text:
Given the following binary number in 32-bit (single precision) IEEE-754 format:
00111110011011010000000000000000
The decimal value closest to this floating- point number is
questions.solution:
Sign 0; exponent 01111100 = 124 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^{124-127}=2^{-3}[/latex]; mantissa 1.1101101[latex]{}_2[/latex] [latex]\approx[/latex] 1.85.

Value [latex]\approx1.85\times\frac18\approx0.23[/latex], closest to [latex]2.27\times10^{-1}[/latex].

Answer: [latex]2.27\times10^{-1}[/latex]

questions.text:
A circular queue has been implemented using a single linked list where each node consists of a value and a single pointer pointing to the next node. We maintain exactly two external pointers FRONT and REAR pointing to the front node and the rear node of the queue, respectively. Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT for such a circular queue, so that insertion and deletion operation can be performed in O (1) time ?

I. Next pointer of front node points to the rear node.
II. Next pointer of rear node points to the front node.
questions.solution:
Insert at REAR (new node after rear) and delete at FRONT. For both in [latex]O(1)[/latex], the rear node's next must point to the front node, which makes the list circular. Front's next points to the second node, not to rear.

Answer: II only

questions.text: The Breadth First Search (BFS) algorithm has been implemented using the queue data structure. Which one of the following is a possible order of visiting the nodes in the graph below?
questions.solution:
BFS from P: neighbours O, Q; then O's new neighbour N, Q's new neighbour M; then M's new neighbour R [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P O Q N M R True

The others break BFS order, e.g. MNOPQR visits O before Q and R, which are M's own neighbours.

Answer: POQNMR
